key_insight: The paper extends an unstructured-grid nonhydrostatic ocean model with a moving generalized vertical coordinate system that can switch between z-level, terrain-following, isopycnal, and hybrid layers to better capture nonhydrostatic ocean flows.
engineering_relevance: This improves the fidelity and flexibility of coastal and ocean simulations where internal waves, stratification, and bottom boundary layers interact on complex geometries.
method: Integrated a generalized vertical coordinate (GVC) framework into the SUNTANS unstructured C-grid nonhydrostatic model.
Added a conservative momentum advection scheme for horizontally unstructured grids.
Developed a positivity-preserving layer-height scheme and tested hybrid coordinates on internal solitary waves.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports validation using turbulent channel flow and application studies on internal solitary waves, showing improved behavior for hybrid coordinates versus z-level or terrain-following coordinates.
watch_item: The approach adds numerical and implementation complexity, especially for maintaining conservation and layer positivity on unstructured moving vertical grids.
paper_title: An unstructured-grid, nonhydrostatic, GVC ocean model Part I: Model description and application of vertical hybrid coordinates to internal solitary waves
